title: Stochastic Token-Window Scheduler for Mixed-Precision Kernel Staggering
creator: Aisha Patel
description:
Problem: For multi-GPU prefills and decode phases we observe recurring microbursts that align poorly with NCCL windows and kernel execution times. Deterministic staggering heuristics reduce tail latency but cause throughput loss and fragile hand-tuned parameters across model shapes and mixed-precision kernels (fp16/int8).

Proposal: Implement a stochastic token-window scheduler that introduces controlled, workload-aware jitter across microbatches and kernel start times to (1) decorrelate token waves from NCCL collective windows, (2) give the kernel selector extra headroom to pick architecture- and precision-specific kernels, and (3) allow attention optimizations (chunking, fused QKV) to better overlap with communication. The scheduler uses lightweight telemetry (per-stage execution histograms + recent NCCL window timing) to sample stagger amplitudes from a bounded distribution per request class.

Key ideas and components:
- Token Window Sampler: per-model/request-class sampler that outputs a micro-delay sequence for tokens/microbatches (bounded by SLO-derived max delay).
- Kernel Hinting Integration: attach jitter metadata to scheduler context so the kernel-selection layer can choose kernels with startup/steady-state characteristics that match the sampled window (e.g., preferring kernels with shorter priming latency when stagger is small).
- NCCL Overlap Policy: monitor NCCL active time; when high overlap contention is detected, the sampler bias increases variance to spread traffic.
- Attention Pathways: coordinate with attention optimization flags (fused QKV / attention chunk size) so the scheduler prefers chunk boundaries aligned with micro-delay windows to maximize compute/comm overlap.

Tradeoffs:
- Adds controlled latency to some requests in exchange for lower tail latency and fewer NCCL collisions. Must quantify net user-facing latency change (p50/p95/p99) and token cost delta.
- Complexity increase in routing/kernal selection logic; must be feature-flagged and gradual rollout capable.
- Edge cases for very short SLOs or single-GPU hosts where stochastic staggering gives no benefit; scheduler must be a no-op there.

Milestones:
1) Design doc & telemetry schema (this ticket) — 2d.
2) Lightweight sampler + perf counters + unit tests behind feature flag — 4d.
3) Kernel hint pass integration (API for scheduler->kernel selector) — 3d.
4) Simulation workloads & lab experiments across heterogeneous GPU types (A100/H100, mixed NVLink topologies) — 5d.
5) Small-scale canary on dedicated pool with rollback and tracing — 3d.

Telemetry & metrics to collect:
- Per-stage kernel start latency distribution (histograms).
- NCCL active time fraction per window, per-device.
- Microburst collision count (attempts where >X comms overlap).
- User-facing latency p50/p95/p99 for canary workloads vs baseline.
- Token/sec throughput and GPU util delta.

Acceptance criteria:
- p99 tail latency for prefills reduces by >=20% on contested multi-GPU workloads with <=5% increase in median latency and <=3% throughput loss.
- No regression on single-GPU or low-concurrency baseline workloads.
- Kernel selection logs show improved kernel-start alignment with NCCL windows (>15% reduction in start-time variance).
- Automated rollback and feature-flag disables in console within 1 minute.

Rollout plan:
- Feature-flag default off. Canary on 2 dedicated pools with mixed topology for 72 hours. If acceptance metrics met, broaden to 10% of dedicated traffic, then to 50% with conservative defaults.

Notes: this approach intentionally avoids deep scheduler determinism; instead it leans on observed distributions to make the runtime robust across model sizes and precision mixes. The kernel-hint API must be minimal: a small enum/hint plus an expected micro-delay window length to keep kernel selector changes low-risk.
